_comment: Ratchet, not a baseline. Tighten these whenever a work package lands; never raise one to make a commit pass. The ScoreEditor caps carry deliberate headroom (see _scoreEditorComment) so that a bug fix is not a budget event; the raises log below is what keeps larger growth honest. Compare module caps encode sprint AC-15 (900 lines without a written ownership justification accepted in review).
_raisesComment: check:debt compares this file against the base ref and fails on any increase that is not declared below with its exact before/after values and a reason. Entries are a permanent log: matching on 'from' as well as 'to' stops an old entry from re-authorizing a later raise. Lowering a budget needs no entry. A raise is for work that genuinely could not fit, not for making a red check green.

raises.reason: SHELL_REDESIGN_DESIGN Phase 0 adds the no-alert rule as a warning (section 8.6) so the 126 alert(), 4 confirm() and 2 prompt() calls left in ScoreEditor and ScoreSection can migrate to the notice service opportunistically; Phase 5 raises the rule to an error. The 132 are existing call sites made visible, not new ones, and this cap is the ratchet that drives them to zero: lower it as each one migrates. The other 3 warnings were already over the old cap of 0.
Same change as the maxWarnings raise above: ScoreEditor.tsx and ScoreSection.tsx now carry no-alert warnings, joining the two files that already had findings.

The compare gap integration needs an explicit queued three-phase engine workflow: establish mismatch breaks, measure and apply wrap resync, then measure and calibrate structural spacers. The pure geometry moved into compare-reflow-plan.ts; the remaining ScoreEditor growth is orchestration and cleanup across the two live WASM score instances.

Same compare gap integration as the line raise above. The added bytes document phase boundaries, pane/score orientation, cancellation, spacer restoration, and the absolute-versus-additive spacer correction that keeps insertions aligned without oscillation.

Selection synchronization and coordinate conversion for the Playwright reliability fixes add explicit state tracking and avoid click, preview, note-input, and paste races. The existing line headroom was insufficient; this restores roughly the same sub-1% working margin without raising the still-unbreached byte cap.

Policy change, not new debt. Pinning to the exact current size made a 41-line bug fix a budget breach and pushed effort into deleting explanatory comments to get back under. Lines are a poor proxy for debt -- a comment costs the same as a mess. This adds ~0.6% headroom so routine work passes while a whole extraction slice of drift still trips it.

Same policy change: ~2% headroom. Bytes remain the metric worth chasing because 500000 is a real threshold (Babel deoptimises code generation above it) rather than a chosen number, and this file is still well above it.

Fixing an AC-14 line breach cost bytes: the clipboard read moved to lib/selection-clipboard.ts, which removes 42 lines from ScoreEditor but leaves a slightly longer call site than the pre-fix code. Lines are the budget that was breached and they are back under it; bytes remain 100,461 under theirs.

TD-07 L2 gates window.__webmscore to non-production builds. The guard is two lines; the rest is the comment recording why a live Score handle on window is not worth its XSS blast radius, and which suites depend on it.
Same change as the maxLines raise above: the production guard on the debug score handle and the comment explaining it.

Bug fix, not new debt: the compare pane viewport status now resolves through an explicit pane/score orientation mapping instead of reading auxiliary-keyed state straight into the right pane. Costs six lines at the call site and moves the rule into compare-pane-status.ts.
Same change as the maxLines raise above: the orientation mapping and the comment recording why it exists.

Ownership move, not new debt: change-review thread creation came back out of CompareDiffGutter, which should not hold the review endpoint or a fetch primitive. The gutter lost 17 lines and four props; the request lives here next to the other change-review calls.
Same change as the maxLines raise above: createChangeReviewThread and the comment stating why the gutter does not own it.

DESIGN_LANGUAGE W3.3 adds the raw-<button> rule as a warning: controls should come from components/ui (Button, IconButton). The 158 are existing call sites made visible (heaviest: ScannerSystemRows 21, PlayerControls 12, CompareDiffGutter 11, ScoreEditor 9), not new ones. This cap is the ratchet that drives them to zero: lower it as each file migrates.
Same change as the maxWarnings raise above: the 37 files that still contain a raw <button>.

Raw-<button> rule (158 existing sites, W3.3), max-lines-per-function at 200 code lines (52 existing functions, W4 S0) and, in W4 S3a, extracted feature hooks (useNotaGenTool 551 lines, useChordTools 548, useTranscodaTool 220, and in S4 useEditorCore ~600) that are themselves over the limit. The user approved this per-hook raise (2026-10-02): a state-heavy hook is a function over 200 lines, moving a cluster out of ScoreEditor's 15,000-line function into one is a net reduction, and the hooks are split further once the core exists (S4). Measured against origin/main, so the changes read as one raise. The ratchet still drives the count down: lower it as buttons migrate and functions are split.

Same changes as the maxWarnings raise above: the 60 files containing a raw <button> or a function over 200 lines. W4 extraction moves existing long functions into their own files (the three S3a hooks, the S4 editor core, and in S3b the 266-line AI patch request, which was already a warning inside ScoreEditor), so the file count rises while the warning count does not.

_scoreEditorComment: Headroom is intentional. These were pinned to the exact current size, and the result was that a 41-line bug fix breached the cap and pressure went into deleting explanatory comments to get back under -- the ratchet making the code worse. Lines are a poor proxy: a comment costs the same as debt. The caps now sit roughly 1% and 1.5% above actual, so routine work passes and a whole slice of drift still trips them. The goal worth chasing is bytes, not lines: Babel deoptimises code generation above 500000 bytes, which this file still exceeds, and that is an observable cost rather than a chosen number.
